note: Window agent p1690-p1699, 2 Nov 2026. Pages opened: Treaty of Ryswick, Treaty of Limerick, Treaty of Karlowitz, Pueblo Revolt, Alxa League (silent), Inner Mongolia, Tuva, Treaty of Nerchinsk.

events.note: 3 October 1691: the Treaty of Limerick 'ended the Williamite War in Ireland'. The draft has held 218 of the island's cells as nobody's since 1662 (the p1700-p1709 patch gives the same reason for 1700); with the Jacobite war over the island is the Crown's Kingdom of Ireland again (the dossier's own 1660-1800 keyframe covers the whole island).

region.text: the area between the Argun River and Lake Baikal, which Russia kept at Nerchinsk

events.note: 27 August 1689: at Nerchinsk Russia 'kept the area between the Argun River and Lake Baikal'. 968 Chita and 20 Buryat cells of that area (inside Cliopatria's 1691 Russian shape) are nobody's in the draft until the 1691 keyframe snap puts them back, so within this window they are nobody's for 1690 only; this gives them to Russia from 1690. Reviewer: the cells are already nobody's at the 1680 anchor (996 Chita cells), so the gap is not made by the 1689 loss event (ledger/73 covers only Amur) and the earlier windows should close it before 1690.

region.text: the area north of the Amur River as far as the Stanovoy Range

events.note: 27 August 1689: at Nerchinsk 'The Russians gave up the area north of the Amur River as far as the Stanovoy Range'. The Qing's own 1689 gain (ledger/29, same region) moves only the 507 cells Russia held; the other 707 cells of the area (364 Amur, 341 Khabarovsk) join the Qing only at the 1691 keyframe snap; this gives them to the Qing from 1690. Reviewer: those 707 cells are already nobody's at the 1680 anchor, not emptied by Russia's 1689 loss event.

region.text: Santa Fe and the Rio Grande pueblos of New Mexico

events.note: September 1692: 'In August 1692, Diego de Vargas marched to Santa Fe unopposed'; he 'arrived at Santa Fe on September 13' and on 14 September 1692 'proclaimed a formal act of repossession'. With the Spanish 1691 keyframe no longer holding New Mexico early, the Spanish Empire's own 1692 gain (ledger/35) would otherwise keep the cells and its 1696 keyframe would strip them; this keeps New Mexico with the viceroyalty from 1692 as in the draft (counterpart spanish-empire so the move works whichever of the two events runs first).

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1691 shape without New Mexico (the Spanish return in 1692); without the Cotabato Valley (Maguindanao) and Buayan's Sarangani Bay core

keyframe_overrides.why: The dossier's correction adds New Mexico 'from 1692' but a keyframe applies from its first year, 1691 (shape years 1691-1695), so the draft gives 1,084 New Mexico cells to Spain a year early. The page: the Spaniards were driven out in August 1680 and 'returned to New Mexico twelve years later'; 'In August 1692, Diego de Vargas marched to Santa Fe unopposed' and on 14 September 1692 'proclaimed a formal act of repossession'. The 1692 return is carried by the ledger (spanish-empire ledger/35, viceroyalty-of-new-spain ledger/4).

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1696 shape without Tuva (Tannu Uriankhai), which the Qing took only in 1758

keyframe_overrides.why: The 1696 shape gives the Qing 571 Tuva cells. The page lists the Khotgoid Khanate and Zunghar Khanate as holders of Tuva for 1634-1758 and says 'In 1758, Tuva came under the Qing dynasty'. Tuva stays nobody's (as the Dzungar keyframes of 1688-1696 draw it); the later Qing keyframes of 1700-1757 carry the same cells (outside this window).

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1696 shape unchanged, applying to 1696-1697 only; plus Freiburg, captured in November 1677 and returned at Ryswick (1697); without the Canadian strip (colonies are cut; New France has its own dossier)

keyframe_overrides.why: The dossier's 1696 keyframe says 'applying to 1696-1697 only' but takes its years 1696-1699 from shapes.csv, so in 1698-1699 the compiler unites it with the corrected 1698 keyframe and the 1698 correction (without Lorraine) is lost: the draft gives France 36 Vosges and Meurthe-et-Moselle cells of Lorraine and 14 Gerona cells at 1698. The page: at Ryswick (September 1697) France returned 'the Duchy of Lorraine to the Holy Roman Empire' and 'evacuated Catalonia, Luxembourg, Mons and Kortrijk'. The override only gives the 1696 keyframe its intended end year, 1697; its correction is the dossier's own.

rulings.why: Cliopatria's Polish shape of 1696 takes Podolia (101 cells) from the Ottomans three years early. The page: at Karlowitz (signed 26 January 1699) 'The Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth recovered Podolia with the undestroyed fortress at Kamianets-Podilskyi', lost 'in the Treaty of Buchach in 1672'; the Ottoman dossier's own 1699 loss event returns it.
